request.system:
You are writing a plain-language summary of an as-filed Tennessee House bill for an adult reader without legal training.

Use only the bill text supplied in the user message. Treat it as a proposal at introduction, not as proof that it became law or describes current law. Do not use outside knowledge, bill descriptions, later legislative history, or the unstated contents of cited statutes.

Write a neutral summary in prose. Start with what the bill would change. Cover its distinct material provisions, including affected people or organizations, new or changed duties and rights, eligibility rules, amounts and thresholds, deadlines, exceptions, reporting or enforcement requirements, and effective dates when stated. Preserve the bill's conditions and legal distinctions; do not turn a permission into a requirement or a proposal into an enacted rule.

Use familiar words and short, complete sentences. Explain a technical term when the supplied text gives enough context; otherwise retain it rather than guess. Distinguish background or WHEREAS statements from operative provisions, and mention background only when it helps explain the bill. If the bill amends or repeals a cited section without showing that section's contents, describe the textual change and citation without inventing the prior rule or its wider effects.

Keep the summary substantially shorter than the source while retaining the main independent changes. A very short bill may need only one or two sentences; a multi-section bill may need several short paragraphs. Do not add opinions, predicted consequences, a readability score, a confidence rating, headings, bullet points, or a list of citations. Return only the fields required by the supplied output schema.

messages.content:
Bill number: HB1153

<bill_text>
SENATE BILL 740
 By Harshbarger

 HOUSE BILL 1153

 By Lynn

 AN ACT to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 49,
 relative to school nutrition.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE STATE OF TENNESSEE:

 SECTION 1. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-6-2302, is amended by deleting

the section and substituting instead the following:

 (a) Each local board of education shall establish a school lunch program and a

 school breakfast program that provides a free lunch and breakfast to each student

 enrolled in a school under the board's jurisdiction who is eligible for free or reduced-price

 meals, according to rules established under § 49-6-2303.

 (b) Subject to available funding, the state shall reimburse each LEA the cost of

 providing a free breakfast and lunch served to each student enrolled in the LEA who is

 eligible for reduced price meals after all federal funds available pursuant to the national

 school lunch program created by the National School Lunch Act (42 U.S.C. § 1751 et

 seq.), the school breakfast program created by the Child Nutrition Act of 1966 (42 U.S.C.

 § 1771 et seq.), or any other federal program have been applied.

 SECTION 2. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-6-2303, is amended by deleting

the language ", regardless of its participation" in subdivision (5) and by deleting subdivision (10).

 SECTION 3. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-2-114(a), is amended by deleting

"receive free or reduced-price school lunches" and substituting "are members of households

with an income that meet the eligibility requirements for free or reduced-price lunch as

determined pursuant to 42 U.S.C. § 1758".

 SECTION 4. This act takes effect July 1, 2025, the public welfare requiring it, and

applies to the 2025-2026 school year and each school year thereafter.
</bill_text>

summary.description: Reader-facing plain-language summary in prose, without a heading or bullet points.

It would replace Section 49-6-2302 so that each local board of education must set up a school lunch program and a school breakfast program. These programs must give a free lunch and breakfast to each enrolled student who is eligible for free or reduced-price meals, under rules set under Section 49-6-2303. Subject to available funding, the state would reimburse each local education agency (LEA) for the cost of a free breakfast and lunch for each student eligible for reduced-price meals. That reimbursement would come only after all available federal funds have been applied. These funds include those from the National School Lunch Act, the Child Nutrition Act of 1966 school breakfast program, or any other federal program. The bill would also amend Section 49-6-2303 by deleting the words ", regardless of its participation" in subdivision (5) and by deleting subdivision (10). The bill does not show what those provisions say. In Section 49-2-114(a), it would replace "receive free or reduced-price school lunches" with wording about students who are members of households with an income that meets the eligibility requirements for free or reduced-price lunch under 42 U.S.C. § 1758.
